title: Engine ticking or tapping
metaDesc: Engine ticking or tapping? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's low oil, lifters, an exhaust leak or normal injector noise, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: tick tick tick from under the hood
engine sounds like a sewing machine
ticking noise that gets faster when I rev
intro: A light ticking or tapping from the engine can be perfectly normal, or it can be an early warning of low oil. The key clues are whether any warning lights are on, what the oil level is, and when the ticking is loudest. Answer the questions below and we'll point you to the most likely cause and the safest next step.
safety: If the oil pressure light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off as soon as it's safe.
If the ticking turns into a deep, heavy knock, stop driving. That can mean serious internal engine damage.
If the check engine light is flashing and the engine shakes, slow down and stop as soon as it's safe.

q_warning.q: Do you notice any of these along with the ticking?
q_warning.help: The oil pressure light usually looks like a red oil can with a drip. A "knock" is a deeper, heavier thud than a tick, more like a hammer than a pen tapping.

opts.a: The red oil pressure light is on or flickering
It's become a deep, heavy knock that gets louder when I press the gas
The check engine light is flashing, or the engine is shaking
None of these, just the ticking

q_oil_level.q: What does the oil dipstick show?
q_oil_level.help: Park on level ground, turn the engine off and wait a few minutes. Pull the dipstick (usually a yellow or orange handle), wipe it, push it back in fully, then pull it out and read where the oil line sits between the two marks. Some newer cars show the oil level on the dash instead.

opts.a: It's below the lower mark, or barely touching it

q_when.q: When is the ticking most noticeable?

opts.a: Mostly right after a cold start, and it fades within a few minutes
A light, fast tick at idle, like a sewing machine, that has always been there
It's louder when I accelerate or climb a hill
Only while the car is moving, and it speeds up with road speed, not engine speed
All the time, warm or cold, and it speeds up when I rev the engine

q_other_signs.q: Does anything else come with the ticking?

opts.a: The engine runs rough, or the check engine light is on (steady)
I smell exhaust under the hood, or hear a puffing sound
No, just a steady tick from the top of the engine

result.title: The engine may not be getting enough oil. Shut it off
result.now: Pull over as soon as it's safe, shut the engine off and check the oil level. Don't restart it until you know the oil is full. If the light stays on with full oil, have it towed.
if: If the oil was very low, adding oil may turn the light off. Even so, have it checked soon, because running low on oil can damage the engine.
If the ticking turns into a knock, don't restart the engine at all.
result.why: The oil pressure light means oil isn't being pushed through the engine with enough force. Ticking along with it usually means the top of the engine is running short of oil. Driving like this can destroy the engine in minutes.

causes.name: Very low oil level
causes.clues: An oil change is overdue, you've seen oil spots under the car, or the engine burns oil.
causes.against: If the dipstick reads full, low oil isn't the cause.

causes.name: Failing oil pump or clogged oil pickup
causes.clues: The oil is full but the light stays on, especially at idle when warm.

causes.name: Faulty oil pressure sensor
causes.clues: The light flickers but the engine sounds normal apart from the tick.
causes.against: Don't assume it's just the sensor until a shop confirms it.

you: With the engine off and cooled for a few minutes, check the oil level on the dipstick.
Look under the car for fresh oil drips.
shop: Mechanical oil pressure test with a gauge
Oil pickup and pump inspection if pressure is low

result.title: A deep knock can mean serious internal engine wear
result.now: Stop driving and shut the engine off. Check the oil level, then have the car towed or have a mobile mechanic listen to it.
if: If the oil is very low, add oil, but don't run the engine to "test" it. A shop should listen first.
If the knock is only a light pinging when you accelerate hard, it may be fuel knock instead. See the engine knocking guide.
result.why: A tick is usually a small part at the top of the engine. A heavy knock that grows with engine speed often comes from worn bearings deep in the engine. Running it can turn a repairable problem into a destroyed engine.

causes.name: Worn connecting rod bearing (rod knock)
causes.clues: A deep, rhythmic knock that gets louder under load and higher engine speed, often after running low on oil.

causes.name: Loose or worn timing chain
causes.clues: A rattle or slap from the front of the engine, often worst at startup.

causes.name: Severe valvetrain wear from oil starvation
causes.clues: The oil was low or very old, and the noise came on quickly.

you: Check the oil level without starting the engine.
Note whether the oil pressure light came on before the noise.
shop: Check the oil and filter for metal particles

result.title: A misfire is likely, and a flashing light means it's severe
result.now: Slow down and pull over when it's safe. Have the car towed or call a mobile mechanic rather than driving on.
if: If the light stops flashing and stays steady, the misfire may have eased, but still get it checked within a few days.
If you smell fuel or see smoke, turn the engine off and step away from the car.
result.why: A flashing check engine light means the engine is misfiring badly enough to send unburned fuel into the exhaust. That can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter. A loose spark plug or ignition problem can also make a ticking or puffing sound.

causes.name: Loose or cracked spark plug
causes.clues: A sharp tick or puff from one spot on top of the engine, often after recent plug work.

causes.name: Failing ignition coil
causes.clues: Shaking that's worst under acceleration, sometimes in damp weather.

causes.name: Fuel injector problem
causes.clues: Rough idle, fuel smell, or poor fuel economy.

you: Note whether the light flashes all the time or only when accelerating.
If you have a code reader, read and save the codes.
shop: Code scan and misfire counter data

result.title: Low oil is the most likely reason for the ticking
result.now: Add the oil type listed in your owner's manual until the dipstick reads full, then listen again with the engine warm. Get the car checked within a few days to find out where the oil is going.
if: If the oil pressure light comes on at any point, shut the engine off and don't drive it.
If the ticking stays after topping up and driving a few miles, have the valvetrain checked. Running low may have worn something.
If you need to add more than a quart between oil changes, the engine is leaking or burning oil.
result.why: The top of the engine is the last place oil reaches. When the level is low, parts like lifters and rocker arms don't get enough oil and start to tick. Topping up often quiets it, but low oil means it's leaking or burning somewhere.

causes.name: Oil leak
causes.clues: Oil spots where you park, or oily residue on the engine.

causes.name: Engine burning oil
causes.clues: Blue smoke from the exhaust, especially at startup, and no visible leak.

causes.name: Overdue oil change
causes.clues: It's well past the oil change reminder or mileage.

you: Top up the oil and recheck the level after a day of driving.
Look under the car and around the engine for oil.
Check when the last oil change was.
shop: Oil pressure test if the ticking continues

result.title: Check the oil level first. It's the most important clue
result.now: Park on level ground, turn the engine off, wait a few minutes and check the dipstick. If it's low, add the oil type listed in your owner's manual until it reads full.
if: If the oil was low and the ticking goes away after topping up, find out where the oil is going within a few days.
If the oil is full and the ticking continues, book a check so a technician can pinpoint the source.
If the oil pressure light comes on, shut the engine off and don't drive it.
result.why: Low oil is one of the most common causes of engine ticking, and also the one that can do the most damage if ignored. It takes two minutes to check and tells you whether this is urgent.

causes.name: Low oil level
causes.clues: An oil change is overdue, or you've seen drips under the car.

causes.name: Noisy lifters or valve adjustment
causes.clues: A steady tick from the top of the engine with full oil.

causes.name: Exhaust leak
causes.clues: Louder when cold or when accelerating.

you: Check the oil level on the dipstick.
Record a short video with sound of the ticking at idle and when revving.

result.title: A tick that fades as the engine warms is usually lifters or a small exhaust leak
result.now: Let the engine idle for 30 seconds or so after a cold start before driving off, and book a check when convenient.
if: If the ticking starts lasting longer or happens when warm too, get it checked sooner.
If you smell exhaust inside the car, get it checked right away. Exhaust fumes in the cabin are dangerous.
result.why: Hydraulic lifters can lose some oil overnight and tick until oil pressure fills them back up. A cracked exhaust manifold or leaking gasket can also tick when cold, then go quiet as the metal heats up and expands to seal the gap.

causes.name: Lifters bleeding down overnight
causes.clues: The tick comes from the top of the engine and is gone within a minute or two.

causes.name: Exhaust manifold leak
causes.clues: A puffing tick from one side of the engine, louder when you accelerate from cold, sometimes with an exhaust smell.

causes.name: Wrong oil thickness or old oil
causes.clues: The tick started after an oil change, or the oil is overdue.

you: Note how long the tick lasts after a cold start.
Check that the oil level is full and the oil type matches your owner's manual.
shop: Cold-start listen with an engine stethoscope

result.title: This may be normal fuel injector or fuel pump ticking
result.now: Check that the oil is full, then listen with the hood open. A steady, light, fast tick that hasn't changed over time is often the normal sound of the fuel injectors.
if: If the tick gets louder, changes in sound, or comes with a check engine light or rough running, book a check.
If you're not sure what's normal for your car, ask a shop to listen to it at your next service.
result.why: Fuel injectors open and close many times a second, and many engines, especially direct-injection ones, make a light ticking sound that's part of normal operation. Some emissions valves click softly too. A noise that's always been there and hasn't changed is usually not a problem.

causes.name: Normal fuel injector noise
causes.clues: A light, even tick at idle that's been there since you've owned the car.
causes.against: If the sound is new or getting louder, something else is more likely.

causes.name: Normal high-pressure fuel pump noise (direct injection)
causes.clues: A ticking from the top of the engine that's more noticeable on a cold engine with the hood open.

causes.name: Evaporative (purge) valve clicking
causes.clues: A soft clicking that comes and goes at idle.

you: Check the oil level.
Compare the sound with a video of the same engine online, or with a similar car.
shop: Code scan if a warning light is on

result.title: An exhaust leak near the engine is likely
result.now: Get it checked within a few days. Until then, drive with the windows cracked open and avoid long trips.
if: If you smell exhaust inside the car, or anyone feels dizzy, gets a headache or feels sick, stop driving and get to fresh air. Have it towed.
If the check engine light comes on, mention it to the shop. A leak can affect the oxygen sensor readings.
result.why: A crack in the exhaust manifold or a leaking gasket lets exhaust puff out each time a cylinder fires, which sounds like a ticking that speeds up with the engine. It often gets louder under load. Exhaust leaks near the engine can let fumes into the cabin.

causes.name: Leaking exhaust manifold gasket
causes.clues: A puffing tick from one side of the engine, louder when accelerating.

causes.name: Cracked exhaust manifold
causes.clues: Louder when cold, quieter when warm, sometimes with a black sooty mark on the manifold.

causes.name: Broken or loose manifold bolt or stud
causes.clues: The noise started suddenly, sometimes after a cold snap.

you: With the engine cold, look for black soot around where the exhaust meets the engine.
Note whether the tick is louder on a cold engine.

result.title: A spark plug or ignition problem may be causing the tick
result.now: Get the codes read and the engine checked within a few days. Avoid hard acceleration and long trips until then.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing, slow down and stop driving as soon as it's safe.
If you smell fuel, stop driving and have it towed.
result.why: A spark plug that's loose or has a cracked insulator can let combustion gas escape, making a sharp ticking or puffing sound along with a misfire. A steady check engine light with rough running points to the ignition system.

causes.name: Loose or damaged spark plug
causes.clues: A sharp tick from one spot on top of the engine, especially after recent tune-up work.

causes.name: Failing ignition coil
causes.clues: Rough running under acceleration, often with a misfire code.

causes.name: Noisy or sticking fuel injector
causes.clues: Rough idle and a fuel smell.

you: If you have a code reader, read and note the codes.
Note whether the roughness is worse at idle or under acceleration.
shop: Spark plug inspection and torque check

result.title: Most likely a noisy lifter or valves that need adjusting
result.now: Keep the oil topped up and on schedule, and book a check when convenient so a technician can pinpoint the source.
if: If the ticking gets louder quickly or turns into a knock, stop driving and have it checked right away.
If the oil pressure light comes on, shut the engine off and don't drive it.
result.why: A steady tick from the top of the engine that follows engine speed usually comes from the valvetrain, the parts that open and close the valves. A worn or sticky lifter, or valves that are out of adjustment, tap with every turn of the engine.

causes.name: Sticky or worn hydraulic lifter
causes.clues: A tick from the top of the engine that may get better or worse with oil changes.

causes.name: Valves out of adjustment
causes.clues: Common on engines with screw or shim-type adjusters, and on high-mileage engines that haven't had a valve adjustment.

causes.name: Worn rocker arm or camshaft
causes.clues: The noise has been slowly getting louder over months.

you: Make sure the oil is full and the right type for your engine.
Record a video with sound at idle and when revving.

result.title: A tick that follows road speed is probably a tire, wheel or brake, not the engine
result.now: Park and look closely at each tire for a nail, screw or stone stuck in the tread, and check the tire pressures.
if: If you find a nail or screw, have the tire repaired or replaced soon, and don't pull it out yourself unless you're ready to fit the spare.
If the clicking is loudest when turning, it may be a worn CV joint. See the clicking when turning guide.
If a tire is losing air or a wheel feels wobbly, don't drive on it. Fit the spare or call roadside assistance.
result.why: If the ticking keeps going when you coast in Neutral and speeds up with road speed, it isn't coming from the engine. Something turning with the wheels is making it, and the most common culprit is something stuck in a tire.

causes.name: Nail, screw or stone in a tire
causes.clues: A steady tick-tick that gets faster as you speed up, sometimes with slow air loss.

causes.name: Worn CV joint
causes.clues: Clicking that's loudest during tight turns.

causes.name: Brake wear indicator or loose brake part
causes.clues: The noise changes when you press the brake.

you: Inspect each tire's tread and sidewall.
Check the tire pressures.
Coast briefly in Neutral on a safe, empty road and listen for whether the tick continues.
